🤔TIMELINES PATTERNS & "Watch What They Build,"

Wars don't start with soldiers. They start with concrete.
You can't fight from a base that isn't built. Bases take years. So if a base is opening today, somebody decided years ago they were going to need it.

Guam is a tiny U.S. island in the Pacific. Closest American soil to China, Taiwan, and the Philippines. Think of it as the front porch.

👊Dec 2022  the Marines opened Camp Blaz on Guam. The first brand-new Marine base in 70 years. Not a remodel. Brand new.
👊Nov 2023  the Coast Guard officially stood up Base Guam. Permanent command, not a temporary post.
👊May 2024 new commander installed over the whole region. Chain of command locked in.

Three big moves. Same island. Eighteen months. That's not random. That's a plan.

Why Marines AND Coast Guard? Marines fight wars. Coast Guard boards ships, seizes cargo, enforces sanctions. One does combat. 
The other does the police work at sea. Together they cover everything from a traffic stop to a shooting war.

Here's the rule: money moves first, then troops. Sanctions, export bans, asset freezes  that's been running for years. The bases opening now are the next chapter, right on schedule.

"First new Marine base in 70 years" is the line that matters. 70 years takes you back to the Korean War. You don't reverse a 70-year plan unless something big is coming.

The concrete was poured before the news started. What you're reading in headlines now was decided years ago by the people pouring that concrete.
Timeline never lies. 
👉Logistics never lies. (Footprint)🦶
Don't watch what they say.
 👉Watch what they build.
@Homeranger17 @CouchGuy17 @X22Report
